t.3.25.1: That great, life-destroying shower of trees and rocks the righteous-souled Rāghava received and countered with his sharp arrows.
t.3.25.2: Taking up that excellent bow, Rāma, like a bull with its eyes half-closed, gave himself over to supreme wrath for the slaughter of all the Rākṣasas.
t.3.25.3: Then, filled with anger and blazing as it were with his splendour, he showered arrows on every side upon the army, together with Dūṣaṇa.
t.3.25.4: Then the enraged commander Dūṣaṇa, the destroyer of foes, seized a hair-raising iron club that resembled a mountain peak.
t.3.25.6: Seizing in battle that iron club, whose touch was like the thunderbolt and lightning, which could shatter the gate-towers of enemies and looked like a great serpent, Dūṣaṇa, the night-roamer of cruel deeds, rushed at Rāma.
t.3.25.5: It was bound with golden bands, a crusher of the armies of the gods, studded with sharp iron spikes and smeared with the fat of foes.
t.3.25.7: As Dūṣaṇa came rushing at him, Rāghava with two arrows cut off both his arms, together with the ornaments on his hands.
t.3.25.8: His hand severed, his huge iron club slipped from him and fell at the forefront of the battle, like Śakra's banner toppling before him.
t.3.25.9: With both his arms scattered, Dūṣaṇa fell to the ground, like a proud, mighty elephant whose two tusks have been shattered.
t.3.25.10: Seeing Dūṣaṇa slain in battle and fallen upon the ground, all beings honored Kākutstha, crying, "Well done, well done!"
t.3.25.11: Meanwhile three enraged commanders who led the army, bound by the noose of Death, banded together and rushed at Rāma: Mahākapāla, Sthūlākṣa, and the mighty Pramāthī.
t.3.25.12: The rākṣasa Mahākapāla raised a huge trident, Sthūlākṣa seized a spear, and Pramāthī took up a battle-axe.
t.3.25.13: But the moment he saw them swooping down upon him, Rāghava received them with sharpened, keen-tipped arrows, as one receives guests who have arrived.
t.3.25.14: Raghunandana cut off the head of Mahākapāla, and with floods of countless arrows he crushed Pramāthin.
t.3.25.15: He filled the two eyes of Sthūlākṣa with sharp arrows; struck down, Sthūlākṣa fell to the ground like a great tree with spreading branches.
t.3.25.17: Those gold-feathered arrows, like fires wreathed in smoke, struck down those rākṣasas as thunderbolts strike down great trees.
t.3.25.16: Then the radiant one, with arrows that resembled fire and were adorned with gold and diamonds, assailed what remained of the rear of that army.
t.3.25.19: By those arrows their armour and ornaments were shattered and their bows were cut and broken, and the night-rangers, smeared with blood, fell down upon the earth.
t.3.25.18: At the forefront of battle Rāma slew a hundred rākṣasas with a hundred barbed arrows, and a thousand with a thousand.
t.3.25.20: With those warriors fallen in battle, their hair loosened and drenched in blood, the whole earth was strewn, like a great sacrificial altar spread with kuśa grass.
t.3.25.21: In but a moment the forest, its rākṣasas slain, became exceedingly dreadful, like hell itself, a mire of flesh and blood.
t.3.25.22: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds were slain by Rāma alone, a mere man fighting on foot.
t.3.25.23: Of that entire army, only the great chariot-warrior Khara and the rākṣasa Triśiras remained, and Rāma, the slayer of foes.
t.3.25.24: Then, seeing that army of terrible strength slain in the great battle by the mighty Rāma, Khara advanced upon Rāma in his great chariot, like Indra with his thunderbolt raised.
